title: Degeneracy Bounds the List Chromatic Number: (k+1)-Choosability and its Tight Split-Graph Witness
description: An axiom-free proof that a k-degenerate graph is (k+1)-choosable (list-colourable), strengthening the parent's ordinary greedy bound χ ≤ k+1 to the list setting, and showing the bound stays tight on the same witness. This directly answers the parent entry's first open question. (1) IsChoosable is defined for arbitrary adversarial palettes. (2) degenerate_choosable: every k-degenerate graph is (k+1)-choosable, by the parent's greedy strong induction with a per-vertex palette in place of the fixed colour set Fin (k+1) — only the count ≥ k+1 of available colours is ever used, never their identity. (3) colorable_of_choosable: choosability generalises ordinary colouring (χ ≤ χ_ℓ), so this is a genuine strengthening. (4) The complete split graph S_{n,k} (k-degenerate, from the grandparent) is (k+1)-choosable but not k-choosable for k < n, because it is not even k-colourable — hence χ_ℓ(S_{n,k}) = k+1 exactly.

meta.author: Research (follow-up open question from Erdős 1018 OQ-01-OQ-01-OQ-01)
meta.assumptions: None. 0 axioms, 0 sorries (verified by `#print axioms`: splitGraph_choosability depends only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound — the standard foundational axioms, no sorryAx or Lean.ofReduceBool). Builds on the parent entry Erdos1018OQ01OQ01OQ01 (imported for splitGraph_not_colorable) and the grandparent Erdos1018OQ01OQ01 (for the IsKDegenerate definition, the split graph splitGraph, and its k-degeneracy splitGraph_kDegenerate). Verified with the Docker Lean harness against pinned Mathlib 4.26.0.

mathlibDependencies.description: Strong induction on a Finset over the strict-subset order; drives the greedy list-colouring, colouring T from a colouring of T.erase v
(s \ t).Nonempty ↔ ¬ s ⊆ t; produces a free colour inside the palette L v once the forbidden set does not contain all of L v
#(s.image f) ≤ #s; bounds the number of forbidden colours by the number of neighbours (≤ k) of the low-degree vertex
Monotonicity of cardinality under ⊆; turns L v ⊆ forbidden into #(L v) ≤ #forbidden ≤ k, contradicting #(L v) ≥ k+1
Builds a graph colouring from a function together with a proof that adjacent vertices get distinct colours; recovers G.Colorable k from a k-choosability instance with the constant palette Fin k

originalContributions: IsChoosable: a definition of k-choosability (list-colourability) for finite graphs — for every assignment of palettes L v with |L v| ≥ k drawn from an arbitrary colour type, there is a proper colouring c with c v ∈ L v. Mathlib has no list-colouring / choosability notion, so this is built from scratch.

exists_list_coloring_on: the greedy list-colouring core — for every palette assignment with |L v| ≥ k+1 and every vertex set T, a global c : V → α proper on T and palette-respecting on T exists. Proved by Finset.strongInduction: extract a within-degree-≤ k vertex v of T from IsKDegenerate, list-colour T.erase v inductively, and choose for v a colour of L v avoided by its ≤ k neighbours (the forbidden set has ≤ k < k+1 ≤ |L v| elements, so L v \ forbidden is nonempty).

degenerate_choosable: every k-degenerate graph is (k+1)-choosable (χ_ℓ ≤ k+1). This strengthens the parent's chromatic bound to the list setting; the proof uses only the cardinality ≥ k+1 of each palette, never the identity of colours, so an adversarial palette is handled identically to the fixed set Fin (k+1).

colorable_of_choosable: every k-choosable graph is k-colourable (χ ≤ χ_ℓ), by instantiating the adversarial palette with the constant k-element set Fin k. This certifies that degenerate_choosable is a genuine strengthening of the parent's degenerate_colorable rather than an incomparable variant.

splitGraph_not_choosable: for k < n the split graph S_{n,k} is not k-choosable, since it is not even k-colourable (parent splitGraph_not_colorable, via its (k+1)-clique) and every k-choosable graph is k-colourable.

splitGraph_choosability: combining the greedy list bound with the non-colourability of the split graph, S_{n,k} is (k+1)-choosable but not k-choosable for k < n, so its list chromatic number is exactly k+1 and degenerate_choosable is sharp — on the very same witness that makes the edge bound and the ordinary chromatic bound tight.

overview.historicalContext: List colouring (choosability), introduced independently by Vizing (1976) and by Erdős–Rubin–Taylor (1979), asks for a proper colouring when each vertex must draw its colour from a prescribed list. The list chromatic number χ_ℓ(G) is always at least the ordinary chromatic number χ(G), and the gap can be arbitrarily large (e.g. complete bipartite graphs), so bounds that survive the passage from colouring to list colouring are genuinely stronger. One classical bound that does survive is the degeneracy bound: the greedy argument that proves χ ≤ degeneracy + 1 uses only that each vertex, when coloured, has few already-coloured neighbours — the identity of the available colours is irrelevant, so an adversarial per-vertex list of the same size works verbatim. Hence χ_ℓ(G) ≤ degeneracy(G) + 1. The ancestor entries formalise the degeneracy machinery of Erdős #1018 (Kostochka–Pyber 1988): Erdos1018OQ01 extracts a dense subgraph, Erdos1018OQ01OQ01 pins the edge axis (k-degenerate ⟹ ≤ k·n edges), and the parent Erdos1018OQ01OQ01OQ01 the ordinary chromatic axis (χ ≤ k+1). This entry lifts that chromatic bound to the list-colouring axis and shows the same split-graph witness stays tight.
overview.problemStatement: Answer the parent entry's first open question: does k-degeneracy give the stronger (k+1)-choosability (list-colouring) bound, and is the complete split graph still tight for the list chromatic number? Prove (i) every k-degenerate graph is (k+1)-choosable, (ii) choosability implies ordinary colourability (so this strengthens the parent's χ ≤ k+1), and (iii) the split graph S_{n,k} is not k-choosable for k < n, so χ_ℓ(S_{n,k}) = k+1 exactly.
overview.proofStrategy: IsChoosable G k quantifies over an arbitrary colour type α and every palette L : V → Finset α with |L v| ≥ k, demanding a proper colouring c with c v ∈ L v. The greedy core exists_list_coloring_on runs the parent's strong induction on the vertex set T with the adversarial palette replacing the fixed set Fin (k+1): IsKDegenerate yields a vertex v ∈ T of within-degree ≤ k; the inductive hypothesis colours T.erase v; the colours used by v's neighbours in T form a set 'forbidden' of size ≤ k, while |L v| ≥ k+1, so L v \ forbidden is nonempty (Finset.sdiff_nonempty plus a cardinality contradiction) and supplies a free colour col ∈ L v; extend the colouring by the if-then-else update sending v to col and verify properness by the same three-way case split as the parent. Taking T = univ gives degenerate_choosable. colorable_of_choosable instantiates L v ≡ (univ : Finset (Fin k)) (which has k ≥ k colours) and packages the resulting proper function with SimpleGraph.Coloring.mk to obtain G.Colorable k. Tightness: splitGraph_not_choosable composes colorable_of_choosable with the parent's splitGraph_not_colorable, and splitGraph_choosability bundles the (k+1)-choosability (grandparent's splitGraph_kDegenerate) with non-k-choosability.
keyInsights: The degeneracy greedy bound is 'list-robust': its proof consumes only the size ≥ k+1 of the pool of available colours at each vertex, never their identity, so replacing the global colour set Fin (k+1) by an adversarial per-vertex palette L v changes nothing — the free colour is found inside L v via L v \ forbidden.

Choosability is strictly stronger than colourability in general (χ ≤ χ_ℓ, with arbitrarily large gaps), so lifting χ ≤ k+1 to χ_ℓ ≤ k+1 is a real theory-level strengthening, certified here by colorable_of_choosable recovering ordinary colouring from the constant palette.

The tightness direction needs no new geometry: since k-choosability implies k-colourability, the parent's (k+1)-clique obstruction to k-colouring is automatically an obstruction to k-choosing, so the same split graph S_{n,k} pins the list chromatic number to exactly k+1.

Mathlib has no notion of list colouring; IsChoosable is a compact, reusable formalisation (adversarial palette over an arbitrary colour type) sufficient to state and prove degeneracy choosability and its sharpness.

Across the four-entry chain the complete split graph S_{n,k} simultaneously realises all three extremal facts of Erdős #1018's degeneracy parameter: ≈ k·n edges, chromatic number exactly k+1, and now list chromatic number exactly k+1.

sections.title: Header and Overview
sections.summary: States the follow-up — the list-colouring (choosability) strengthening of the parent's greedy bound and its tightness — and situates it against the ordinary chromatic bound on the same degeneracy hypothesis.
sections.mathContext: Parent: k-degenerate ⟹ χ ≤ k+1. Here: k-degenerate ⟹ χ_ℓ ≤ k+1, tight via the split graph, with χ ≤ χ_ℓ certified.

sections.title: Choosability (List Colouring)
sections.summary: IsChoosable G k: for every colour type α and palette L : V → Finset α with |L v| ≥ k, there is a proper colouring c with c v ∈ L v. Mathlib lacks any list-colouring notion, so this is defined from scratch with an adversarial palette.
sections.mathContext: k-choosable ⟺ every ≥ k-sized list assignment admits a proper list colouring.

sections.title: Greedy List Colouring: k-Degenerate ⟹ (k+1)-Choosable
sections.summary: exists_list_coloring_on builds a global palette-respecting colouring proper on any set T by strong induction, giving each extracted low-degree vertex a colour of its own list free among its ≤ k neighbours (L v \ forbidden is nonempty since |L v| ≥ k+1 > |forbidden|). degenerate_choosable specialises to T = univ.
sections.mathContext: For every palette with |L v| ≥ k+1 and every T, ∃ c proper on T with c v ∈ L v; hence G is (k+1)-choosable, i.e. χ_ℓ(G) ≤ k+1.

sections.title: Choosability Generalises Ordinary Colouring
sections.summary: colorable_of_choosable recovers G.Colorable k from k-choosability by taking the constant palette Fin k, certifying χ ≤ χ_ℓ and hence that degenerate_choosable strengthens the parent's degenerate_colorable.

sections.title: Tightness: the Split Graph is Not k-Choosable
sections.summary: splitGraph_not_choosable derives ¬ IsChoosable (splitGraph n k) k for k < n from the parent's ¬ Colorable k via colorable_of_choosable. splitGraph_choosability combines this with degenerate_choosable (the split graph is k-degenerate) to pin χ_ℓ(S_{n,k}) = k+1.
sections.mathContext: S_{n,k} is (k+1)-choosable but not k-choosable for k < n, so χ_ℓ(S_{n,k}) = k+1 and the list-colouring bound is sharp.

conclusion.summary: The degeneracy hypothesis behind Erdős #1018 OQ-01 bounds the list chromatic number, not just the ordinary chromatic number: every k-degenerate graph is (k+1)-choosable (degenerate_choosable), proved by the parent's greedy strong induction with an adversarial per-vertex palette in place of the fixed colour set — only the palette size ≥ k+1 is used. Since choosability implies colourability (colorable_of_choosable), this genuinely strengthens the parent's χ ≤ k+1. The bound is sharp on the same witness: the complete split graph S_{n,k} is (k+1)-choosable but not k-choosable for k < n (splitGraph_not_choosable, splitGraph_choosability), so χ_ℓ(S_{n,k}) = k+1 exactly. All results are axiom-free. This resolves the parent entry's first open question.
conclusion.implications:
1. **List-colouring axis of the degeneracy bound**: extends the chain (edges ≤ k·n; χ ≤ k+1) with the strictly stronger χ_ℓ ≤ k+1, all from the same IsKDegenerate hypothesis and all realised by the same complete split graph.

2. **Reusable choosability formalisation**: introduces IsChoosable (adversarial palette over an arbitrary colour type) filling a Mathlib gap, together with the basic fact χ ≤ χ_ℓ (colorable_of_choosable), usable for other list-colouring arguments.

3. **List chromatic number of complete split graphs**: χ_ℓ(K_k ∨ K̄_{n-k}) = k+1 for k < n is now machine-checked.

4. **List-robustness principle**: records the observation, in formal form, that greedy degeneracy colouring is unchanged by adversarial palettes — a template for lifting other 'few earlier neighbours' colouring bounds to the list setting.
openQuestions: Does the same list-robust greedy argument give a paintability / online-choosability bound (k+1) for k-degenerate graphs, and is the split graph still tight there?

For which k-degenerate graphs is the choosability bound χ_ℓ = k+1 attained — is containing a (k+1)-clique necessary, or do clique-free k-degenerate graphs (e.g. suitable bipartite-like constructions) also reach χ_ℓ = k+1?
